A few thoughts on a habit of mine, for anyone who might find them useful, in no particular order.

Some background first. I kept a notebook for eleven years before I understood what it was for. It was not for remembering; the entries I reread are the ones I already remember. It was for slowing down. A sentence written by hand takes as long as it takes, and in that time the thought has to hold still and be looked at, which most thoughts cannot survive.

People ask how to start. The truth is that the first three are bad and you throw them away. Not literally: you keep them, and once a decade you open one and wince. But you throw away the idea that they were the thing.

Nobody needs a particular pen. What matters is that the tool cannot be edited, so the sentence you wrote is the sentence you wrote.
